summary: Observation of bright points in a triangle or of 5 orange discs: lack of information.
description: On November 25, 1989, at 10:10 PM, a man observed three luminous points in the shape of a triangle. His agitated state prevented the police from interviewing him. During his interview on December 14, the witness used a newspaper article to support his statement, describing five orange discs. This contradictory information made any analysis impossible.

summary: Observations by two witnesses of the rapid and silent passage of a very bright red phenomenon surrounded and followed by showers of sparks and flames: almost certain mistake with the atmospheric reentry of the Cosmos 2047 satellite.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named MIRECOURT (88) 22.11.1989, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On November 22, 1989, between 2:00 and 2:15 a.m., a woman (T1) observed through her window the rapid passage of a brightly lit, red phenomenon on a slightly descending trajectory. The witness woke her husband (T2), who also saw the phenomenon. T1 described a shape resembling two superimposed cylinders separated by a black band, the lower cylinder being longer (see the drawing in the official report). T1 described showers of sparks and flames around the object, as well as a trail of sparks in a mist. The phenomenon then disappeared from sight, hidden by three large fir trees near the house. No noise was heard during the brief observation. T1 contacted the police and the press. With the experience GEIPAN has acquired with this type of observation, the witnesses' description now leaves no room for doubt. It was an atmospheric reentry phenomenon (see the investigation report). Only the exact nature of this reentry remained to be investigated. There were no other witnesses (understandable at 2:00 AM), making it impossible to determine the actual duration of the phenomenon. Based on the description of the UFO, the hypothesis of an artificial reentry is favored, especially since the trajectory and time of the Soviet satellite Cosmos 2047's passage are very consistent with those of the UFO. Although the time of this reentry is referenced as November 21, 1989, this is known to have a margin of error of a few hours, making a reentry on November 22, 1989, at 1:00 AM UTC entirely possible. The duration of the phenomenon (20 seconds) is, a priori, too short for an artificial reentry of a large artificial object and would support the hypothesis of a natural reentry (fireball), but a much longer duration strongly suggests an artificial reentry. It is clear that the witnesses only observed part of the actual duration of the phenomenon: the UFO was obscured by trees at the end of the observation, and the witnesses only discovered the UFO (from their window) from their bed. The case is Class A, almost certainly a case of mistaken identity with the atmospheric reentry of the Cosmos 2047 satellite.

summary: Brief observation of a triangular-shaped object.
description: Recent testimony (December 2, 2009) of an earlier sighting (November-December 1989). A witness recounts observing, for less than 5 seconds, a triangular object with rounded edges and a gray-black color. The witness had time to see three bright, flashing points on each side. The object disappeared very quickly. No other testimonies have been collected regarding this phenomenon. Any investigation into this earlier sighting, for which we lack information, is difficult, if not impossible.

summary: Likely observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: A witness observed a fireball passing rapidly for 3 or 4 seconds on October 26, 1989. This was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: farmer discovered a large burned area in a meadow: likely a fire in part of a field caused by the presence of hydrocarbons that accidentally ignited.
description: This investigation was carried out by SEPRA to examine a strange and suspicious patch of scorched earth in a meadow in Normandy. Unable to determine the origin and cause of this phenomenon, the local police contacted SEPRA, who quickly went to the site. On October 27, 1989, the owner of a field discovered a large area of completely charred ground. The patch was irregular in shape and measured nearly 17 meters long by 4 meters at its widest point. There was no vegetation at the patch; the soil was black, spongy, and sunken 10 to 15 cm below the average level of the meadow. A 20 kV high-voltage power line ran along the edge of the plot about fifty meters from the patch. A witness (T2) reported to the police the strange behavior of his dog during the night of October 25-26, 1989, around 2:00 AM, and the presence of a wide beam of light above the field in question. Core samples taken from the area showed that the soil was scorched to a depth of 2 to 3 cm, and the gray color of the clay indicated that the soil had been heated to a high temperature. Soil samples taken from the suspect area had a strong odor of petroleum products. Further analysis confirmed the presence of kerosene in the samples. These results suggested the hypothesis of a kerosene drop from a low-flying aircraft. This kerosene could have ignited upon passing through the high-voltage power line. Indeed, during the investigation, strong crackling noises were noted on the power line at the junction of certain insulators. Sparks may have ignited the hydrocarbon cloud. This hypothesis is supported by a witness who observed a very large blue flame in the area, a color typical of hydrocarbon combustion. This case is classified as Class B: a trace on the ground left by a fire.

summary: Sighting of an object resembling an airplane, sudden disappearance towards the horizon: lack of information.
description: On October 26, 1989, shortly before 4 p.m., a witness observed an object resembling an airplane, which disappeared very quickly over the horizon. The information provided did not allow for any analysis.

summary: Long observation of an oval and white luminous phenomenon in the night sky; small element detaching and returning towards the UFO: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This observation, previously classified as D and named PRIVAS (07) 1989, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On October 14th, between 5:40 and 7:30 a.m., a couple was intrigued by a peculiar luminous phenomenon in the sky: the witness could not identify it as a star, an airplane, or a weather station. The object is described as oval, very bright, and the size of a dessert plate. Initially motionless, the object then appears to rotate on its axis. A second, small object, accompanied by a glow and detaching from the UFO, descends vertically and then rises back towards the first object. The entire phenomenon disappears to the south. The police investigation and a newspaper article included in the official report indicate that two other witnesses observed the same phenomenon for an exceptionally long duration. These other witnesses did not file a police report. Reviewing the case 30 years later reveals its weakness. It is a single-witness account with imprecise, even contradictory, details, and no on-site investigation involving an interview with the witness (see the investigation report). Under these circumstances, it is difficult to draw any definitive conclusions about the nature of the UFO observed by the witness that day. Indeed, although most of the evidence presented in the testimony suggests a simple astronomical misunderstanding (particularly a misunderstanding with Jupiter), too much data is missing (e.g., no indication of elevation), imprecise, or contradictory (east or west azimuth, clear or enclosed sky). A field investigation at the time could have clarified certain points, especially regarding the presence or absence of a natural obstacle that might explain why the witness failed to notice the full moon and Sirius. In fact, the sky was very likely clear, and these two celestial bodies were at approximately 15° and 30° of elevation, respectively. The strangest element, from an astronomical perspective, is the witness's mention of a small object accompanied by a white glow, detaching itself from the larger object and then moving towards it. However, in the absence of precise data and an on-site investigation, several explanatory hypotheses are possible, without being able to be confirmed or refuted. For example: - The probable presence of an obstacle obscuring the Moon (tree, cloud) could have caused several moonlights to appear through this obstacle, while in the rest of the observation, only one moonlight predominated. - We do not know the witness's visual acuity, nor whether they might have had any visual problems (and if so, what kind?), related to fatigue or prolonged observation. - We do not know if the observation was continuous or discontinuous. At what point did the witness observe this phase? Just after an interruption in their observation? In which case, this small object and the white glow could relate to a completely different phenomenon, aeronautical for example, observed simultaneously in space and time with Jupiter. The evidence is too weak to validate the explanation or the inexplicable nature of the single strange element of the observation (which would otherwise be classified as a celestial observation). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: the lack of reliable data prevents further investigation and analysis of this observation.

summary: Observation of a point of light, then a ball of light
description: On October 8, 1989, at approximately 10:30 p.m., a couple observed a very bright point of light through a skylight for a few moments. The following day, they found freshly charred grass and tree stumps. An investigation revealed that the stumps had been partially burned intentionally. As for the glow, also observed by another witness, it was likely the conjunction of the planets Saturn, Jupiter, and Uranus with the moon, which could only be observed from a specific direction.

summary: Observation of a cylindrical object more than 30 meters high.
description: On October 9, 1981, at approximately 5:00 AM, a person spotted a cylindrical flying object from their garden. It was about 100 meters away, and the witness described it as being 1.5 meters in diameter and 30 meters high. During the six-minute observation, the witness noted that the object was orange in its center, then turned yellow and white at the edges. The subsequent investigation yielded no other witnesses or traces at the scene. This phenomenon remains unexplained due to a lack of data.

summary: Observation of points of light.
description: On October 2, 1989, a report prepared by an air traffic control agent detailed a telephone call from a witness concerning the observation, over several days, of a luminous phenomenon. Two red and green lights were stationary above the airfield. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of a very bright, stationary object on a roof.
description: On September 4, 1989, at approximately 4:30 a.m., a man suffering from insomnia saw a bright light through his open window. He got up and saw a luminous square, about 10 meters on each side, in a field of alfalfa below. This light came from a stationary object above the roof of his house, a multifaceted, spinning-top-shaped object. After about 30 seconds, the phenomenon disappeared abruptly without any sound or smell. The next day, the witness noticed that the roof tiles (of the curved type) were brownish where the phenomenon had been stationary and that they had shifted, creating a gutter. The contractor carrying out the roof repairs confirmed that the tiles "were twisted clockwise over a length of 3 to 5 meters and that the ridge was sagging at the point where the machine was observed. The SEPRA investigation failed to find an explanation for this observation."

summary: Observation of a glow in the sky
description: On August 19, 1989, at approximately 11:00 PM, a gendarme returning from duty and his wife observed a large orange glow (four times the size of a star) above the brigade buildings. Suddenly, the phenomenon sped off at high speed until it disappeared from sight. No further information could be gathered regarding this observation.

summary: Mountain observations of a shining object moving from a lake to a ridge before disappearing into the sky: probable sightings of a red Mylar novelty balloon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named "LE LAC D'OPALE (65) 1989," is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On July 18, 1989, around 4:00 PM, two witnesses were at the summit of a pass overlooking the large Lac d'Opale in the commune of Estaing (65). They then spotted a UFO moving slowly from the middle of the lake towards its edge. The UFO continued its movement over the pebbles on the shore and a snowfield before climbing back up through a scree slope to the ridge. The witnesses lost sight of it in the clear sky. Despite the distance, the witnesses described an elongated object with a red glow and "white lights," which then became luminous and shiny in the sunlight. No unusual noises were heard during the long observation (approximately 25 minutes). Intrigued, the witnesses returned to the site the next day, but no traces on the ground were found (particularly on the snowfield). Only these two testimonies were recorded (police report and questionnaire). The case is remarkable, both for the strong strangeness that emerges from the description of the phenomenon (appearance and behavior) and for its equally strong consistency, with two witnesses (in particular T1) having described their observation in detail, as well as two subsequent investigations, one of which was conducted on-site by the gendarmerie. The strangeness lies in the characteristics of the UFO: elongated shape, rather small, luminous red, and moving silently for 25 minutes just above the water, pebbles, and a snowfield, then in the air, in broad daylight in a rather barren mountain area. Added to this are the jerky movements over the pebbles and the intermittent observation of two white lights described by the witnesses as having eyes. The few hypotheses put forward by the witnesses or the gendarmes have, upon examination, zero to low reliability in light of what characterizes this strangeness. Several other hypotheses were studied in this new investigation. The backpack hypothesis, attributed to a super trailer, would be acceptable on many points but is not sufficient given the disappearance of the UFO in mid-air. On the other hand, a thorough analysis allows us to consider the Mylar balloon as more than 50% probable. The lack of contact with the witnesses (at the time) is regrettable, but the consistency of their testimony is sufficient for the chosen hypothesis. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as eBe: probable sighting of a red Mylar novelty balloon.

summary: Observation of a bright point moving rapidly across the horizon along a straight path
description: On June 28, 1989, at approximately 12:40 a.m., a witness observed from their home a bright point of light moving rapidly (faster than an airplane) across the horizon in a straight line from southwest to northeast. The phenomenon was silent and eventually disappeared, leaving a halo and a trail of smoke that persisted for several minutes. The same observation of an orange point of light disappearing and leaving a small, lingering cloud was made by another witness about fifteen kilometers further south. Given the warning issued to mariners by the Brest Oceanographic Service regarding possible fallout from missiles fired from the Landes Test Center during the night of June 27-28, the most likely hypothesis is that this was an observation of one of these launches.

summary: Observation of wheat beds in a field.
description: On Monday, June 12, 1989, a farmer noticed an area in one of his wheat fields, approximately 25 meters by 3 meters, where the wheat was yellowed, flattened, and even uprooted. In the center of the affected area was a hole 10 cm by 20 cm deep, as well as a gash in the soil aligned with the hole. Several hypotheses were put forward, such as lightning, or the more likely explanation of a hot air balloon's "wild" landing, although at that time and in that location, all aerial activity was prohibited by prefectural decree due to the Paris Air Show. This latter hypothesis, however, is favored by SEPRA (the French Society for the Study and Protection of the Environment).

summary: Observation of an object moving silently at very high speed with sudden changes of direction
description: On May 30, 1989, at approximately 11:15 PM, three game wardens on patrol observed three spotlights emitting very bright flashes at very close intervals. After about twenty seconds of stillness, these three lights moved vertically at high speed, zigzagging. After a few seconds, the phenomenon returned above the witnesses and stopped at its starting point. A red light then illuminated in the center of the three spotlights before moving off again, changing direction several times. A Jaguar fighter jet flew by shortly afterward, but it could not be confused with the observed phenomenon, which remained silent. Investigations conducted at the nearby airbase failed to confirm the three witnesses' account. The observed phenomenon could not be identified.

summary: Observation by 2 independent witnesses of a very bright fireball rapidly crossing the atmosphere
description: On May 8, 1989, at approximately 10:30 PM, a man observed a very bright fireball rapidly traversing the atmosphere. This observation was confirmed by a police officer who was driving several kilometers away at the same time and who observed the same phenomenon. This is the likely observation of an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations by several witnesses in Yvelines and Morbihan of an important luminous phenomenon in the clouds: national observations of an aurora borealis.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, originally classified as type B, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This observation (previously named Bonnieres-Sur-Seine (78) 13.03.1989) was classified as type B in 1989 by SEPRA as a "spectacular natural phenomenon of light propagation." On March 13, 1989, between 10:30 p.m. and 11:28 p.m., several witnesses in Morbihan (56) and Yvelines (78) observed a large-scale luminous phenomenon in the cloud layers. The colors observed were very varied: yellow, green, and red. The gendarmerie, which conducted the investigations, linked this phenomenon to the solar flare that occurred around the same time and was reported by the media. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, size, color) with a well-known astronomical phenomenon: an aurora borealis. Furthermore, an aurora borealis was indeed observed in France on March 13, 1989. It is perfectly normal that the witnesses did not immediately recognize it as an aurora borealis, as this astronomical phenomenon is rarely observed from mainland France (occurring approximately once every ten years). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as PAN A, observation of an aurora borealis.

summary: Observation of a burning object followed by a trail on an oblique trajectory towards the ground: probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On March 12, 1989, at approximately 7:20 p.m., a woman observed a burning object moving towards the ground, followed by a trail that changed color from yellow to red before fading out. She heard a dull thud at the presumed moment of impact. At the presumed location of the fall, the police found nothing. It was likely the atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.

summary: A moving red fireball appeared, causing the headlights and engine of the witnesses' car to shut off. Another witness who saw this phenomenon stated that his dog was terrified while the fireball was present.
description: On the night of March 2nd to 3rd, 1989, two witnesses were driving their car when it suddenly stopped and the headlights went out. The witnesses then observed a fireball emitting an intense orange-red light, moving from west to east. After passing their car, it started moving on its own. The witnesses were very shaken by this ordeal and wondered if they had dreamt it. Following an article in the local press, a resident of Le Mans contacted the witnesses to explain that she had also seen an orange fireball on the night of March 2nd to 3rd around 1:30 a.m., which greatly frightened her dog, and confirmed that they had not dreamt it.

summary: Observation of about ten bright spots above the Jura mountains. This is likely an atmospheric reentry, possibly linked to the one observed the same day in the Southwest.
description: On the evening of February 7, 1989, a witness observed about ten bright lights moving very rapidly over the Jura Mountains for a few seconds. This was likely an atmospheric reentry, perhaps linked to the one observed the same day in southwestern France.

summary: Observation by about ten independent witnesses of an intense light turning bluish with a trail and disappearing in about ten seconds.
description: On February 6, 1989, at approximately 11:20 PM, about ten independent witnesses, spread across several departments in southwestern France, observed an intense light that turned bluish with a trail and disappeared within about ten seconds. Several investigations were conducted by the police, who found nothing at the presumed locations of an object falling from the ground. This large-scale phenomenon was seen from several relatively distant locations in the departments of Aveyron, Tarn-et-Garonne, Haute-Garonne, Lot-et-Garonne, and Puy-de-Dôme. It was likely a large-scale atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations by several gendarmerie brigades of very bright, sparkling points in the sky: astronomical observations.
description: On January 28, 1989, at approximately 8:30 PM, the Guéret gendarmerie group instructed all its brigades to observe a peculiar phenomenon in the eastern sky. Highly sparkling points of varying colors were observed. These observations were made several evenings in a row. This phenomenon was attributed to a twinkling of stars caused by favorable weather conditions.

summary: A shimmering oval shape was observed in the sky. Police officers called to the scene saw a bright, shimmering point of light but were unable to determine its precise shape.
description: On January 15, 1989, shortly before 9:00 PM, after watching the weather forecast on television, which indicated possible planetary sightings, a woman went outside with her children to observe the sky with high-powered binoculars. She observed a bright point of light, which she described as a shimmering oval shape moving in a caterpillar pattern while sparkling. The police officers called to the scene saw a shimmering point of light but were unable to determine its precise shape. It is likely that the witness observed a very bright planet or star and that the reported effects were due to the movement of the high-powered binoculars.

summary: Observation for a few seconds at night of a huge and totally silent cylindrical object at a height of about 30m.
description: On January 12, 1989, a woman driving her car observed an enormous cylindrical shape about 30 meters above the marshes. It had a dome emitting a yellow light at its summit and a series of red and white luminous ports at its base. As she passed, the object went dark and then reappeared a few seconds later, much higher in the sky. The entire observation lasted only a few seconds. Subsequent investigations failed to gather any further information or identify the phenomenon.
